title: Ketchup Chicken Fried Rice under a Folded Omelette
summary: A Japanese home-style favourite of chicken and vegetable fried rice tossed in tomato ketchup and butter, shaped into neat mounds and draped with a soft, fully set omelette. A zigzag of ketchup and some parsley finish it off.
equipment: nonstick frying pan with a lid (20 cm)

ingredients.item: cold cooked short- or medium-grain rice (from about 170 g raw)
boneless skinless chicken thigh, in 1.5 cm pieces
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Fry the vegetables
steps.text: Break the cold rice into separate grains. Heat the oil in the large pan over medium-high heat, add the onion and carrot and cook for 3 minutes until the onion is translucent. Softening the vegetables first gives them time to sweeten before the rice goes in.

steps.title: Cook the chicken
steps.text: Add the chicken and cook for 4-5 minutes, stirring, until browned on the outside and cooked through (74°C). Small, even pieces cook quickly and stay juicy, and the browning adds savoury flavour to the rice.

steps.title: Season the rice
steps.text: Add the butter, then the rice, and cook for 2 minutes, breaking it up, until glossy. Stir in the ketchup, soy sauce and pepper and cook for 1-2 minutes until the rice is evenly coated and piping hot (74°C), then stir in the peas for 1 minute. Briefly frying the ketchup caramelises its sugars, giving a deeper, less sharp tomato flavour.

steps.title: Shape the mounds
steps.text: Lightly oil the small bowl, pack in half the rice, turn it out onto a plate and lift off the bowl. Repeat on the second plate. Pressing the rice firmly gives a neat dome that holds its shape under the omelette.

steps.title: Make the omelettes
steps.text: Whisk the eggs, milk and salt until smooth. Melt 10 g butter in the small pan over medium heat, pour in half the egg and stir quickly with a spatula for 20-30 seconds until small curds form. Spread it level, cover and cook on low for 1-2 minutes until fully set with no liquid egg left on top (71°C). The lid traps gentle steam, setting the surface through while the base stays tender and pale.

steps.title: Drape and serve
steps.text: Slide the omelette onto one rice mound, tucking the edges under to wrap it neatly, then repeat with the remaining butter and egg. Pipe or zigzag the ketchup over the top, scatter with parsley and serve at once, while the rice is hot.

tips: A common mistake is cooking the omelette over high heat, which browns and toughens it; keep the heat medium, then low under the lid.
Use cold, day-old rice so it fries into separate glossy grains instead of clumping.
Have the rice mounds ready on the plates before you start the omelettes, as they cook in just a few minutes.
Stir the curds quickly at first for a fine, even texture before levelling the egg.
storage: Cool quickly, refrigerate within 1 hour and use within 24 hours. Reheat once only until piping hot (74°C) throughout; the omelette is best made fresh. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
